title_en: Shenzhen Peiqi Import and Export Trade Co., Ltd. v. Hubei Bank Co., Ltd., Yichang Nanhu Branch, and Huacheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of bankruptcy claims
ruling_gist_en: 1. A non-party cannot apply for retrial under Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, because that provision applies only to the parties listed in the effective judgment and their universal successors in interest. Pursuant to Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law in the Trial Supervision Procedure, one of the constitutive elements for a non-party to apply for retrial is that the non-party can claim rights over the subject matter of enforcement as determined by the original judgment, ruling, or mediation statement. The phrase 'can claim rights over the subject matter of enforcement' as used herein does not include the situation of having a creditor's right over the subject matter of enforcement.

full_text_en:
Shenzhen Peiqi Import and Export Trading Co., Ltd. v. Hubei Bank Co., Ltd. Yichang Nanhu Sub-branch and Huacheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of bankruptcy claims

Ruling Summary

1. A person not a party to the case cannot apply for retrial under Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, because the application of that article is limited to the parties specified in the effective judgment and their successors in rights and obligations. In accordance with Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, one of the constituent elements for a person not a party to the case to apply for retrial is that such person can assert rights over the subject matter of execution determined by the original judgment, ruling, or mediation statement; the ability to assert rights over the subject matter of execution as referred to herein does not include the circumstance of holding a creditor's right over the subject matter of execution.

2. Although the effective judgment or enforcement ruling has determined that a company's shareholder shall bear supplementary compensation liability to the company's creditors for the portion of the company's debt that cannot be satisfied, within the scope and interest of the insufficient capital contribution, if the company has been declared to enter bankruptcy proceedings before the shareholder actually bears the supplementary compensation liability, then in accordance with Articles 16 and 35 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the PRC, the shareholder shall first make up the capital contribution to the company. The capital contribution so made up can only be used for fair distribution among all creditors of the company, and cannot be used for repayment to individual creditors.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling (2012) Min Shen Zi No. 386

Applicant for Retrial (Person not a party to the case): Hubei Bank Co., Ltd. Yichang Nanhu Sub-branch (formerly Yichang City Commercial Bank Nanhu Sub-branch). Address: No. 16 Longkang Road, Yichang City, Hubei Province.
Person in Charge: Wang Shouzhen, President of this Sub-branch.
Agent ad litem: Deng Yiping, lawyer of Hubei Baiste Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Ran, intern lawyer of Hubei Baiste Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shenzhen Peiqi Import and Export Trading Co., Ltd. Address: Rooms 3601, 3603, Building 3, Binjiang, No. 30 Hongling South Road, Futian District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.
Litigation Representative: Administrator of Shenzhen Peiqi Import and Export Trading Co., Ltd.
Person in Charge of Administrator: Zheng Liangzhen.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Huacheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. Address: No. 2 Dahua Road, Dongcheng District, Beijing.
Litigation Representative: Bankruptcy Administrator of Huacheng Investment Management Co., Ltd.
Person in Charge of Administrator: Wang Bin.

The applicant for retrial, Hubei Bank Co., Ltd. Yichang Nanhu Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Nanhu Sub-branch), dissatisfied with the civil judgment No. 853 (2011) Gao Min Zhong Zi of the Beijing High People's Court in the case of dispute over confirmation of bankruptcy claims against the respondents Shenzhen Peiqi Import and Export Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Peiqi Company) and Huacheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huacheng Company), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

Nanhu Sub-branch applied for retrial on the grounds that: The judgment of the second instance found that the bankruptcy administrator of Huacheng Company (hereinafter referred to as Huacheng Administrator) should not have confirmed Nanhu Sub-branch's claim, which in effect deprived Nanhu Sub-branch of its right to file a claim. 1. This judgment effectively negated the ruling of the Yichang Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Yichang Intermediate Court) No. 110-4 (2000) Yi Zhong Fa Zhi Zi, which lawfully added Huacheng Company as an enforcee, and also negated the opinions of the coordination meeting presided over by the Supreme People's Court, attended by multiple courts including the Beijing High People's Court, for unified enforcement of this case. Therefore, it negated Nanhu Sub-branch's status as a creditor of Huacheng Company, resulting in Nanhu Sub-branch being unable to file a claim with the Huacheng Administrator, as the enforcee, in accordance with the Yichang Intermediate Court's ruling and the Beijing High People's Court's decision. 2. The Yichang Intermediate Court's ruling No. 110-4 (2000) Yi Zhong Fa Zhi Zi has already taken legal effect, making Huacheng Company a joint and several debtor of Peiqi Company. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law) and the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases, Nanhu Sub-branch is lawfully entitled to file a claim with Huacheng Company as a joint and several debtor for the entire debt, and this right of Nanhu Sub-branch is an obligation of Huacheng Company. 3. The Beijing High People's Court, in the absence of Nanhu Sub-branch, deprived Nanhu Sub-branch of its rights in the "Opinion of the Court" section, violating the principle of legitimacy in court adjudication. 4. The judgment of the second instance applied Articles 16, 17(1), 30, and 35 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law in handling this case, which constitutes an erroneous application of law. 5. The judgment of the second instance found that the Huacheng Administrator violated Article 17 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law by wrongfully discharging property to the debtor's debtor, which is improper, because Huacheng Company was declared bankrupt in 2009, whereas the Yichang Intermediate Court ruled that Huacheng Company bore responsibility in 2001. Nanhu Sub-branch applied for retrial of this case pursuant to Article 179(1)(6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Opinion of the Court: Nanhu Sub-branch applied to this Court for retrial in the capacity of a person not a party to the case, and therefore Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC cannot be applied, because the application of that article is limited to the parties specified in the effective judgment and their successors in rights and obligations. Articles 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC clearly provide for the elements for a person not a party to the case to apply for retrial. Pursuant to the above provisions, there are two main elements for a person not a party to the case to apply for retrial: first, the person not a party to the case must be able to assert rights over the subject matter of execution determined by the original judgment, ruling, or mediation statement; second, no new lawsuit can be filed to resolve the dispute.

As can be seen from the facts found at first and second instance in this case, both Nanhu Sub-branch and Peiqi Company hold claims against Huacheng Company, and the underlying causes of these two claims are the same, i.e., both are based on Huacheng Company's failure to make full capital contributions to Peiqi Company and its corresponding obligation to make up the capital contribution. The focal point of the dispute is the ownership of the 14 million yuan bankruptcy claim in question. 1. According to the Yichang Intermediate Court's civil judgment No. 6 (2000) Yi Zhong Jing Chu Zi and its civil ruling No. 110-4 (2000) Yi Zhong Fa Zhi Zi, Huacheng Company shall bear liability to Nanhu Sub-branch within the scope of its insufficient capital contribution, but the enforcement proceeding had not been completed before the people's court accepted the bankruptcy case. Because bankruptcy proceedings are a general enforcement of all of the debtor's property, focusing on fair satisfaction of all claims, they have exclusivity over general debt satisfaction procedures. Therefore, after Peiqi Company and Huacheng Company were successively declared bankrupt, any preservation measures or enforcement measures taken against Huacheng Company's property, including those taken pursuant to the Yichang Intermediate Court's civil ruling No. 110-4 (2000) Yi Zhong Fa Zhi Zi, constitute unenforced property and must be suspended according to law. Bankruptcy property shall be fairly distributed in the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings. 2. Registered capital is the property guarantee for a company to bear civil liability to all its creditors. Where a shareholder has not made full capital contributions, if the company is declared to enter bankruptcy proceedings, according to Article 35 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, which provides that "after the people's court accepts a bankruptcy application, if the contributor of the debtor has not yet fully performed its capital contribution obligation, the administrator shall require the contributor to pay the capital contribution it has subscribed, without being subject to any time limit for capital contribution," Huacheng Company, as a shareholder, shall first make up the capital contribution to Peiqi Company. Pursuant to Article 30 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, this made-up capital contribution shall constitute part of the bankruptcy property of Peiqi Company and can only be used for fair distribution among all creditors of Peiqi Company, and cannot be used for repayment to individual creditors; otherwise, it would contravene Article 16 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, which provides that "after the people's court accepts a bankruptcy application, any repayment of debts by the debtor to individual creditors is void," and would infringe upon the lawful interests of other creditors of Peiqi Company. Therefore, the judgment of the second instance, which confirmed that the bankruptcy claim in dispute belongs to Peiqi Company, is consistent with the spirit of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. Nanhu Sub-branch may file its bankruptcy claim with Peiqi Company and participate in distribution. In summary, Nanhu Sub-branch's grounds for retrial application, that the judgment of the second instance found that the Huacheng Administrator should not have confirmed Nanhu Sub-branch's claim, thereby effectively depriving Nanhu Sub-branch of its right to file a claim, and that the judgment of the second instance erroneously applied the law, are all untenable.

Because the 14 million yuan bankruptcy claim in dispute belongs to Peiqi Company, Nanhu Sub-branch can no longer assert rights over the above bankruptcy claim, which is the subject matter of this lawsuit. Therefore, it cannot apply for retrial of the effective judgment in this case in the capacity of a person not a party to the case. In accordance with Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, it is ruled as follows:

The application for retrial of Hubei Bank Co., Ltd. Yichang Nanhu Sub-branch is dismissed.
